source: Source: U.S. Dept. of Transportation, "Bumping & Oversales"

scenes.text: You're at the gate. Ticket in hand. And they say: sorry, no seat.
scenes.head: SORRY, NO SEAT

scenes.text: What?! You PAID for that seat!
scenes.head: I PAID FOR THAT!

scenes.text: Here's the thing. Airlines may sell more tickets than seats. The Department of Transportation says it's legal.
scenes.head: MORE TICKETS THAN SEATS

scenes.text: They're betting somebody won't show up.
scenes.head: IT'S A BET

scenes.text: When everybody does... first, they ask for volunteers.
scenes.head: STEP ONE: VOLUNTEERS

scenes.text: Bumped anyway? You can be owed up to four times your one-way fare.
scenes.head: BUMPED ANYWAY?

scenes.say: The cap: twenty-one hundred fifty dollars.
scenes.head: THE CAP

scenes.text: So... cash, or seat? Decide now, because one day...
scenes.head: CASH OR SEAT?
